title: Crisis test tracks fire_tick but never asserts the fire-after-resolve ordering it claims to pin
detail: fire_tick is assigned but never read afterward. The header's contract — the fire lands after crisis resolution — is never asserted; saw_resolve only proves resolution happened at some point.
recommended_fix: Also capture the Crisis_Resolved tick and assert fire_tick >= resolve_tick, or delete fire_tick entirely.

title: era_test_catalog_3 is a no-op: both call sites discard its return and test_catalog already stops at era 3
evidence:
+era_test_catalog_3 :: proc(cat: ^Catalogs, allocator := context.allocator) -> ^Catalogs {
+	cat3 := era_test_catalog(cat, allocator)
+	pop(&cat3.eras) // era 4 was the last row — drop it
+	return cat3
+}

+	cat := test_catalog(&cat_storage)
+	era_test_catalog_3(cat) // eras 1-3 only — a fired era 2->3 leaves the gate inert

+	make_era_row(cat, 1, "foundations", "Foundations (ARPANET)", 1, {ei2}, {res2, rt2}, {na2, std2}, allocator)
+	make_era_row(cat, 2, "email_web", "Email & Web", 2, {ei2}, {res2, rt2, sb2}, {na2, std2}, allocator)
+	make_era_row(cat, 3, "streaming_surge", "The Streaming Surge", 3, {ei2, si2}, {res2, rt2, sb2, ch2, cp2, rm2, rh2}, {na2, std2, wd2}, allocator)
detail: Both callers discard the return. test_catalog already builds exactly rows 1-3, so the append-era-4-then-pop round-trip nets zero on the fixture actually used — dead scaffolding whose comment claims it matters.
recommended_fix: Delete era_test_catalog_3 (test_catalog is already the 3-row table) or actually assign its result at the call sites.

title: Milestone window is never re-armed after a fire — consecutive eras can advance one tick apart
detail: No ring/window reset exists on the fire path anywhere in the diff. The entered era inherits an already-elapsed window full of the previous era's traffic — a healthy era-1 gate-on run can cascade 1→2→3 on consecutive ticks, skipping each era's sustain contract.
recommended_fix: Reset the gate ring and re-anchor the window at the fire tick (per-era sustain), or explicitly pin single-advance-per-run semantics.

title: Density check misses duplicate era rows — a duplicate silently overwrites and passes
detail: Rows are written indexed by era, so two rows claiming the same era overwrite one slot and the table stays dense — the silently dropped row defeats the "every row must be a real row" claim.
recommended_fix: Reject duplicate (and non-advancing) era numbers in the parse loop at write time, not only post-hoc index equality.

title: Window-elapsed precondition duplicated in two places with two different tick sources
detail: Same precondition implemented twice: era_step reads the tick parameter, era_gate_sla_ok reads state.tick. The inner copy is unreachable via era_step and diverges silently if the two sources ever disagree.
recommended_fix: Keep the check in exactly one place (era_step) reading one source; delete the duplicate inside era_gate_sla_ok.

title: Re-step hazard handled oppositely from the adjacent growth feature: gate accepts ring data loss
evidence:
+// safety: the diff (prev_* scratch) sees delta 0 on a re-step — the accepted
+// 4.2 convention (the ring slot may be overwritten with zeros on a same-tick
+// re-step; the harness drains per step, the app never re-steps, replay never
+// re-steps, so replay equality holds).

 The same-tick re-step guard: the pre-existing step_once test convention re-steps a tick, and a re-step must not re-plan + re-apply growth (the rng would not have advanced between the two calls, so a re-plan could find a SECOND valid spot and double-spawn).
detail: Growth adds an explicit re-step guard because re-steps are a known codebase convention; the new gate instead accepts a zeroed ring slot on re-step. Any re-stepping caller with the gate enabled silently loses window data.
recommended_fix: Mirror growth's guard: record the last-updated tick in Era_Gate_State and make a same-tick re-step a no-op.
